# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

The paper asked whether what a network trained on squared error gets wrong when it forecasts an autoregressive series is a bias or only the information it lacks, in a setting where the two can be told apart exactly.

H1 is {{< var h1.decision >}}: the largest model with the full window is equivalent to Bayes on {{< var h1.n_equivalent >}} of {{< var h1.n_total >}} verdicts, with every {{< var design.level_pct >}}% interval of excess error within [{{< var h1.mse.min_lo >}}, {{< var h1.mse.max_hi >}}] points and every interval of the gap within ±{{< var h1.gap.max_abs_end >}}, against margins of ±{{< var design.margin.mse >}} and ±{{< var design.margin.gap >}} (@sec-h1). For H2, the decision at each of W = {{< var design.windows_finite >}} is "{{< var h2.w2.decision >}}", with {{< var h2.w2.n_equivalent >}}, {{< var h2.w4.n_equivalent >}}, {{< var h2.w8.n_equivalent >}} and {{< var h2.w16.n_equivalent >}} of {{< var h2.n_total >}} verdicts equivalent to window-Bayes and the widest interval end at {{< var h2.all.mse.widest_end >}} points of excess error and {{< var h2.all.gap.widest_end >}} of gap (@sec-h2). H3 is {{< var h3.decision >}}: {{< var h3.statement >}}; the largest upper end of a {{< var design.level_pct >}}% interval is {{< var h3.max_hi >}} against the {{< var design.h3.threshold >}} threshold (@sec-h3). Nothing was flagged, so the re-training at {{< var design.steps_long >}} steps was not run.

Read together, the three say that the largest network, trained to the end of its schedule, forecasts like a Bayesian with the same window at every memory length tested, within the registered margins. Judged against the truth it overreacts at low persistence and underreacts at high persistence, by amounts as large as the effects reported for people; judged against the forecaster with its information it does neither, within margins a small fraction of those effects. The slope diagnostic of the expectations literature, applied to it with the full-information forecast as the reference, would report biases that are, within the registered margins, the information limit. The revision diagnostic shows the same pattern, though no margin was registered for it (exploratory). That is the paper's methodological point, and it does not depend on the networks: it is visible in the benchmarks alone (@fig-benchmarks, @tbl-benchmarks).

The qualifications are part of the result. Equivalence holds at step {{< var design.steps >}}, when the learning rate has reached zero, and not at {{< var design.step_mid >}} steps. Window-Bayes is the squared-error optimum, so what has been shown is that finite training reached it with no residual in the human direction, for one architecture on simulated data. The smallest model does not reach it and errs towards a middling persistence, which at high persistence is the opposite of the human signature. At ρ = 0 even the largest model overstates persistence by a few thousandths, inside the margin. And in the unknown-mean setting closest to the laboratory, the matched Bayesian itself overreacts at high persistence and the human intervals include the four-observation curve, so the descriptive overlay does not show people overreacting beyond an information-limited Bayesian (@sec-overlay).

Three extensions would test how far the result reaches. The first is the pair of arms dropped here: a prior at evaluation that differs from the prior in training, and a break in persistence in mid-sequence, both of which take the network away from the case in which the Bayes forecast under the training prior is the right benchmark. The second is training itself: other schedules, shorter budgets and architectures without an output head affine in the current value, with the equivalence tracked along the whole learning curve and the evaluation-set error quantified by a bootstrap. The third is the human side: fitting the window and the prior of an information-limited Bayesian to the experimental forecasts themselves, instead of overlaying a curve from a window fixed in advance, would turn the descriptive overlay into a test.
